title: Follower Onix rams its captured Wild Pokémon target

verification.actor: Current level50 Follower Onix and level50 Wild Snorlax on Route29.
verification.trigger: Place Snorlax off the follower line, finish native setup, bind both full current owners, then use normal Right16 input to enter the line. Wait four neutral frames for capture, then use Left32 to move the player away while the follower charges its saved Wild target.
verification.observable: Condition49626 in Ram captures the full current Wild target. Its first native Walk goes toward that target current tile. Onix completes shared Walk travel and control return. One accepted contact reduces real resident Snorlax HP by33, then one shared forced23-frame Jump moves it three tiles, shows an airborne arc, lands and returns control. Player saved HP and attacker real party HP do not change.

setupMutations.change: Teleport on private ROM/save copies, prepare and release party Onix, spawn Wild Snorlax, settle one native frame and bind both exact identities. No profile, motion, condition, HP or RNG writes during observation.
Normal Right16, neutral4 to capture the target, Left32 to move the player away, then neutral input; read saved player HP at each end.

limits: Prepared party and placement do not prove natural follower selection or population acquisition.
This focused case proves the Follower attacker and Wild victim; existing Wild Ram tests retain their separate player target and Crash cooldown claims.
The target must remain alive and have an open three-tile Jump destination. A short or blocked Jump does not pass.
Current native memory and semantic receipts supply proof; no screenshot or sound-from-speakers claim.

events.value: Bind inactive current follower and full-health Wild victim after native setup.
Use normal Right16 to enter the target line, neutral4 to capture it, then Left32 to move the player away.
Observe captured-target charge, real HP loss, completed Jump3 and16 tail frames.

stop.condition: Finish one captured-target charge and real33-HP hit with complete Jump3 and16 tail frames; fail at the first owner, target, direction, HP, movement or control error.

invariants: The Follower owns the authored Ram condition and captures one current Wild Pokémon.
First charge direction uses the current captured target position.
One common movement path provides charge and forced Jump; full native samples and control returns are required.
The player and attacking party Pokémon retain HP.
